clue.text: Oil firm going about work on well, rapidly moving object

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece put on another follows it

parts.note: hale means healthy, in good health

indicators.note: going about says one piece goes around another, enclosing it

parts.note: BP is the British oil company
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A petroleum company is busy working near a well, with something racing past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rapidly moving object' is a coy way of describing the great comet of 1997; 'going about' signals the wrap and 'on' the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Hale-Bopp was the bright comet of 1997, a celestial body travelling at great speed.

clue.text: Game and wine upset old solvers

parts.note: hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

indicators.note: upset in a down answer turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: ye is the old form of you, the solvers being addressed

explanation.surface: A game and some wine end up upsetting elderly puzzlers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hockey is a team sport played with sticks and a ball or puck.

clue.text: French article put forward case: right to leave union

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article

indicators.note: to leave says that letter departs from the word, removing it

parts.note: to argue is to put forward a case

explanation.surface: A French piece of writing argued that the right should quit a union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To leave' removes R from ARGUE, giving AGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is an alliance or association of parties joined together.

clue.text: Fantastic fish brought to one worker

parts.note: brill is a flatfish
I is the Roman numeral one
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords

explanation.surface: A wonderful fish is handed over to a single employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant is used informally to mean wonderful or superb.

clue.text: Ridiculous trousers start to expand, and pop undone

indicators.note: undone suggests things unfastened and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Absurd: the trousers begin to expand and the button pops open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undone' shuffles TROUSERS, E (from 'start to expand') and POP together.
explanation.definitionFit: Preposterous means absurd, contrary to reason or common sense.

clue.text: Bacon pieces?

parts.note: Francis Bacon wrote a famous collection of short prose pieces, not rashers of meat

explanation.surface: Slices of bacon, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Bacon is not the meat but Francis Bacon, the English philosopher, whose best-known work is a book of short prose compositions.
explanation.definitionFit: Short prose compositions are what Francis Bacon published under that title in 1597.

clue.text: Bayonet in male side

definitions.meaning: to bayonet is to stab or run through with a pointed weapon
the male line of a family is called the ... side, so this word appears in that phrase

explanation.surface: A soldier is stabbed with a bayonet on the man's flank.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a fill-in: the word goes in front of 'side' to make the term for the male line of descent, as opposed to the distaff side.
explanation.definitionFit: A bayonet thrust stabs like a lance; the paternal branch of a family is the spear side.

clue.text: Flowering maple left in U-boat at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flowering plant has been left aboard a German submarine out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' rearranges L, IN and UBOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Abutilon is a shrub of the mallow family, called flowering maple for its maple-like leaves.

clue.text: Rise in this? Flood barriers up to protect nearly everything

indicators.note: to protect says one piece wraps around and shields another
up in a down answer means the word reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: levees are embankments built to stop rivers flooding

indicators.note: nearly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Will waters climb here? Flood barriers are raised to keep almost everything safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' reverses the embankments to SEEVEL, 'nearly' trims, and 'to protect' wraps. The question mark flags a definition by example: rising seas.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate change is expected to raise the ocean's surface height, so this is what would go up.

clue.text: Instrument at home opening red wine

indicators.note: opening says one piece cuts into another, entering it

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
in means at home

explanation.surface: A musician at home is opening a bottle of red.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a woodwind instrument with a single reed.

clue.text: Bartok perhaps eating sides off enormous whale

indicators.note: eating says one piece swallows another, holding it inside

parts.note: Bela Bartok was the Hungarian composer, so Bela is an example of a first name

indicators.note: sides off means the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: huge means enormous

explanation.surface: A composer is seen consuming a gigantic whale, minus its flanks.
explanation.walkthrough: Bartok's first name is the target, not the composer himself; 'sides off' trims and 'eating' wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: The beluga is the small white Arctic species of cetacean.

clue.text: After wasted hour go a long way in the road

indicators.note: in says the wordplay sits inside the word the
after says the distance piece follows the scrambled letters
wasted means ruined or spoiled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
far means a long way

explanation.surface: Having lost an hour, you must travel a great distance down the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' scrambles two words into OROUGH; 'in the' looks like part of the definition but places everything inside the word 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughfare is a main street or public way through a place.

clue.text: As in Rome to stop the Spanish getting even

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so one piece fills the middle of another

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of

explanation.surface: As the Romans do, they try to halt the Spaniards and settle the score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As in Rome' points to Latin rather than the proverb; 'to stop' means plugging the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and equal are synonyms for level or matching in amount.

clue.text: Mum, not married, sensible under different conditions

indicators.note: not says that letter is absent, removed from the word

parts.note: mother means mum
wise means sensible

explanation.surface: A single mother is prudent in changed circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes M from MOTHER, leaving OTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise can mean if things were not so, in other circumstances.

clue.text: Tour de force from principal oarsman

parts.note: master means principal, as in a master copy or a school's head
the stroke is the rower who sets the pace in a boat

explanation.surface: A brilliant feat by the lead rower of the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: The stroke is the rower seated nearest the stern who sets the rhythm for the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterstroke is a brilliant achievement, as is a tour de force.

clue.text: Reprimanded and removed from list

definitions.meaning: this sense means scolded or told off
this sense means marked as done with a check mark against an item

explanation.surface: Scolded and struck off the register.
explanation.definitionFit: Being told off sharply, and an item checked off a to-do list, share the same phrase.

clue.text: Fish beneath rocks to glide on frozen pond

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece beneath another comes after it

parts.note: on the rocks means with ice, so rocks is slang for ice
skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A fish swims under rocks, while others slide over a frozen pond.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice-skate is to move across ice on bladed boots, gliding over a frozen surface.

clue.text: House one French girl in Cockney district

indicators.note: in says these pieces sit inside the district's name

parts.note: Bow is the East London district; a true Cockney is born within the sound of Bow bells
un is French for one
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A home for one French girl in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is in London's East End, the Cockney heartland.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a single-storey dwelling.

clue.text: Knock back drink on bar

indicators.note: in an across answer a piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: a counter is the bar over which drinks are served
punch is a mixed drink

explanation.surface: Down a drink sitting on the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' suggests swallowing a drink, but here it is a blow struck in return.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterpunch is a retaliatory blow, a hit given back in a boxing exchange.

clue.text: Mountain, cold in two areas, and beast there?

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

indicators.note: in says the letter is placed within the pair

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, so two of them give AA
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: High peaks, chilly zones, and an animal roaming them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the surface: this animal lives in the high, cold Andes, hence 'there'.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a domesticated South American camelid of the Andean highlands.

clue.text: Picnic in light wind

definitions.meaning: this sense means something easy, as in no picnic
this sense means a gentle wind

explanation.surface: An outdoor meal in a gentle wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done with no effort is a doddle or cinch; a soft wind is also called by this word.

clue.text: Wise man having confrontation in plant

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
a brush is a brief encounter or clash, as in a brush with the law

explanation.surface: A wise man has a run-in among the shrubbery.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagebrush is an aromatic shrub of the North American desert.

clue.text: Dim market speculator holds onto pound

indicators.note: holds onto says one piece clasps another inside it

parts.note: a bear sells shares expecting prices to fall
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: A gloomy trader clings tightly to his money.
explanation.definitionFit: Blear means blurred or misty, so faint or indistinct.

clue.text: English monarch beheaded calculating Swiss

indicators.note: beheaded says the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a ruler is a monarch

explanation.surface: An English king has his head cut off, as a scheming Swiss looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calculating' looks like 'scheming' but means a mathematician: Leonhard Euler, the great eighteenth-century Swiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was a prolific Swiss mathematician, a man who did a lot of calculating.

clue.text: Please to be cooked like kippers

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are prepared and transformed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A request for some smoked herring to be prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: Kippers look like smoked fish but are people having a kip, British slang for a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A kip is a nap in British slang, so those having one are sleeping.

clue.text: Lowly nobles in pub on time

parts.note: a bar is a pub
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Minor aristocrats drinking in the tavern punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: Barons form the lowest rank of the British peerage, and the baronage is them collectively.

clue.text: Longshanks in some measure unleashed war dogs

indicators.note: in some measure says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A long-legged warrior lets slip the dogs of war.
explanation.walkthrough: Longshanks was the nickname of the English king Edward I, who was very tall.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward I of England was nicknamed Longshanks for his height and long legs.

clue.text: Gateau served with red meat in hunks

parts.note: beef is red meat
a gateau is a rich cake

explanation.surface: A dessert comes with a steak course at the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefcake is slang for muscular, attractive men displayed for their physiques.
